title: A Geometry of Admissible Seams: Contract-Bound Invariants and Auditable Transitions
object_of_study: geometric representation of transitions and seam admissibility under frozen contracts
main_question: How can heterogeneous transitions be represented geometrically while keeping admissibility dependent on explicit contract and seam conditions rather than scalar resemblance?

claim_layers.claim: The note states that the kernel is domain-agnostic by construction, not reducible to a single score, and that admissibility is grounded in identity closure across seams under a frozen contract (deposited PDF, December 18th, 2025).

The note treats cross-domain transfer as an empirical property rather than an assumption and states portability criteria: disclosed embedding/mapping, reproducibility, seam viability, closure stability under reuse, consistent admissibility behavior, and a quantified failure boundary, with a practical reporting minimum of manifests, closure registries, and audit rows.
The library places this as historical candidate material under UMCP; the historical/current seam is preserved, not reconciled.
